summary: Lists junit callback parameters: fail_on_change, fail_on_ignore, hide_task_arguments, include_setup_tasks_in_report, output_dir (default ~/.ansible.log), replace_out_of_tree_path, task_class, task_relative_path, and test_case_prefix.
questions: Where does the junit callback write its XML files?
How do I make changed tasks count as JUnit failures?
How do I hide task arguments in the JUnit report?
Can I exclude fact-gathering setup tasks from the JUnit report?
How do I only treat some tasks as test cases?
Do ignored failures show as failures in JUnit output?

answer_card.title: junit callback parameters
answer_card.answer_md:
- `fail_on_change` (false): treat `changed` tasks as failures
- `fail_on_ignore` (false): treat failed tasks as failures even with ignore_errors
- `hide_task_arguments` (false, 2.8): hide task arguments
- `include_setup_tasks_in_report` (true): include setup tasks
- `output_dir` (default `~/.ansible.log`): directory for the XML files
- `replace_out_of_tree_path` (none, 2.12.3): placeholder for out-of-tree relative paths
- `task_class` (false): one class per YAML file
- `task_relative_path` (none, 2.8): use paths relative to this directory
- `test_case_prefix` (empty, 2.8): only tasks with this name prefix are test cases; failing tasks are still recorded as failed test cases
